hypotheses.justification: Neither collision nor definedEquality requires finiteness of its domain: both test existence of a shared defined value. Only A is summed over. The existing proof works unchanged without this instance, including empty B (the pointwise argument requires no inhabitants).

collision is the classical decision of ∃ y, f p.1 = some y ∧ f p.2 = some y, and definedEquality is its real-valued indicator; neither definition requires finite Y. The existing case-split proof works unchanged. If Y is empty, the existential is false and both sides are zero. This instance and [Fintype B] can also be removed together.
